name: Iron Maiden Eddie's Blend Darkest Red Wine Art #2
text:
## Iron Maiden Eddie's Blend Darkest Red Wine Art #2 [lcbo-39936]

**The wine and the band**

This is a [Douro](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Douro+Valley,+Peso+da+Regua,+Portugal&t=k) red made for the British heavy metal band [Iron Maiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Iron+Maiden&go=Go). Its name comes from the band's 2021 song Darkest Hour, and it is a Douro DOC red sourced from the Van Zeller Wine Collection ([The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2024/03/iron-maiden-strikes-a-chord-with-new-douro-doc-wine/)). That song is from the album [Senjutsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Senjutsu+album&go=Go) ([Wikimetal](https://www.wikimetal.com.br/en/iron-maiden-launches-red-wine.)).

The "Eddie" on the label is [Eddie the Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Eddie+Iron+Maiden+mascot&go=Go), the band's skeletal mascot. "Wine Art #2" is a label-art edition; [Tesco Ireland](https://www.tesco.ie/shop/en-IE/products/317760438) sells the same Wine Art #2 bottle. The LCBO listing doesn't state a vintage, so check the back label: the critic score below is for the 2021.

**The producer**

The bottle says it is produced and bottled by The Wine Collection S.A. in Vila Nova de Gaia ([Tesco Ireland](https://www.tesco.ie/shop/en-IE/products/317760438)), the port-lodge town across the river from Porto ([map](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Vila+Nova+de+Gaia,+Porto,+Portugal&t=k)). That company is the Van Zeller Wine Collection, the renamed former Barão de Vilar, Vinhos SA ([The Yeatman](https://www.the-yeatman-hotel.com/en/wine/partners/the-wine-collection/)).

Fernando and Álvaro van Zeller started that port house in 1996, a few years after their family sold Quinta do Noval to AXA Millésimes in 1993 ([vintageport.se](https://www.vintageport.se/house/BaraoDeVilar.php)). [Quinta do Noval](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Quinta+do+Noval,+Pinhao,+Portugal&t=k) sits above [Pinhão](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Pinhao,+Alijo,+Portugal&t=k). Some press reports credit Van Zellers & Co, the house run by their cousin [Cristiano van Zeller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Cristiano+van+Zeller&go=Go); the bottle's own label points to the Wine Collection.

**The grapes**

The blend is [Touriga Franca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Touriga+Franca&go=Go), [Tinta Roriz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Tempranillo&go=Go), [Tinto Cão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Tinto+C%C3%A3o&go=Go) and [Touriga Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Touriga+Nacional&go=Go), the main Douro grapes for both [port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Port+wine&go=Go) and table wine. For the 2021, Touriga Franca was 40% and Touriga Nacional 30% ([Kork](https://lbv.kork.ca/en/our-wineries/van-zellers-co/iron-maiden-darkest-red/2021)).

Part of the wine spends time in port barrels, which adds a little richness before bottling ([Tesco Ireland](https://www.tesco.ie/shop/en-IE/products/317760438)). The LCBO lists it at 13.5% alcohol and 12 g/L of sugar, styled medium-bodied and fruity ([LCBO](https://www.lcbo.com/en/iron-maiden-deepest-darkest-red-blend-39936)).

**What the reviewers say**

[Decanter](https://decanter.com/wine-reviews/portugal/douro-valley/iron-maiden-eddies-blend-darkest-red-douro-valley-2021-90096) gave the **2021 vintage 90 points**. Tina Gellie tasted it in London in October 2024 and set a drinking window of 2024–2028. In her view, the port-barrel time gives a rich, spicy wine with dark fruit to match the name.

Among shoppers, [Ocado](https://www.ocado.com/products/iron-maiden-darkest-red/639197011) shows an average of 3.7 out of 5 from 10 reviews, with no vintage given. I found no CellarTracker notes for this wine, and no critic reviews of the newer 2023 or 2024 vintages.

**Practical note**

Drink it now; it's built for early drinking, and Decanter's window for the 2021 runs to 2028. No decanting needed, though 20 minutes in a jug or a large glass will open it up. [Vinoscout](https://www.vinoscout.de/en/collections/iron-maiden) suggests serving at 16–18 °C, which is cooler than most rooms, so 15 minutes in the fridge helps.

The touch of sweetness and soft tannin suit smoky, savoury food. Try it with [feijoada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Feijoada&go=Go) made with chouriço, a grilled burger or [ribeye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Ribeye+steak&go=Go), or [alheira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Alheira&go=Go) sausage with fried potatoes.

**From the history books**

- **1620:** The van Zeller family came to Portugal from the Netherlands in the early 17th century and has worked in the Douro since 1620 ([Essential Algarve](https://www.essential-algarve.com/home-page-header-stories/400-years-of-history-cristiano-van-zellers-journey-through-douro-wines/)).
- **1703:** The [Methuen Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Methuen+Treaty&go=Go) between Portugal and England secured the British market for port ([Wine with Seth](https://www.winewithseth.com/winewiki/douro-valley/)).
- **1756:** A royal charter of 10 September 1756 demarcated the port-growing region, making the Douro the world's first formally demarcated wine region ([Wikipedia](https://EN.wikipedia.com/wiki/Douro_DOC)). This was the work of the [Marquis of Pombal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Marquis+of+Pombal&go=Go).
- **1836:** Queen [Maria II of Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Maria+II+of+Portugal&go=Go) made Cristiano Nicolau Kopke the 1st Baron of Vilar, a title the family still holds ([Garrafeira Nacional](https://www.garrafeiranacional.com/en/kaputt-branco.html)).
- **2024:** The wine was launched at [ProWein](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Messe+Dusseldorf,+Dusseldorf,+Germany&t=k) in March 2024 with importer Ehrmanns Wine, after a year in development ([The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2024/03/iron-maiden-strikes-a-chord-with-new-douro-doc-wine/)).

**Curious details**

The rock matters. Douro [schist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Schist&go=Go) splits vertically, so vine roots can push deep between the plates for summer moisture; growers traditionally broke up the bedrock before planting ([Wine with Seth](https://www.winewithseth.com/winewiki/douro-terroir-schist-soils/)).

The climate is Mediterranean, with very cold winters and very hot, dry summers ([Quinta do Vallado](https://www.quintadovallado.com/en/vineyards/)). Pombal marked the original boundary with 335 granite pillars, which can still be seen ([Wine with Seth](https://www.winewithseth.com/winewiki/douro-valley/)).

Each grape adds something. Tinto Cão is a low-yielding variety that brings spice to the blend ([Ocado](https://www.ocado.com/products/iron-maiden-darkest-red/639197011)). The 12 g/L of sugar the LCBO lists is unusually high for a dry Douro red; my reading is that it softens the tannins and explains the smooth, plush feel.

The packaging was a joke that sold. The Eddie artwork came from the band's Future Past tour, and the importer quipped that the bottle was a gift for lazy people because it came already wrapped ([The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2024/03/iron-maiden-strikes-a-chord-with-new-douro-doc-wine/)). According to Portuguese outlet NiT, it sold more than 600,000 bottles in 30 countries ([NiT](https://www.nit.pt/comida/gourmet-e-vinhos/iron-maiden-lancam-novo-vinho-produzido-no-douro-e-a-garrafa-e-de-colecao)).

## Ranking by reviews
1. Iron Maiden Eddie's Blend Darkest Red Wine Art #2 — $19.95 at LCBO — 90 points, Decanter (Tina Gellie), 2021 vintage.
My own rating is 87. The Decanter 90 is a single review of the 2021, and the 3.7/5 from shoppers is lukewarm. It's a well-made, crowd-pleasing Douro red, but you're paying a few dollars for the label.
